sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Luzerne County?
sections.html:
Two layers handle it. The county Assessment Office decides what each parcel is worth, and the municipality and school district where the parcel sits apply their own millage rates to that figure. The county's property tax page says the bill depends on the assessed value from Luzerne County's Assessment Office combined with the mileage rates of your municipality and your school district.

With 76 municipalities in the county and a dozen school districts, two houses with the same assessment can carry different yearly bills. The districts include Wilkes-Barre Area, Hazleton Area, Wyoming Valley West, Pittston Area, Dallas, Crestwood, Greater Nanticoke Area, Hanover Area, Lake-Lehman, Northwest Area, Wyoming Area and Berwick Area. Find your taxing bodies on your bill before you compare prices with a house in the next town.

The Assessor's Office is in the Courthouse Annex at 153 North River Street, Wilkes-Barre, and takes calls at 570-825-1540. Its hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A branch in Hazleton keeps Tuesday and Thursday hours from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Mail to the appeals board goes to 200 North River Street, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Luzerne County assessment?
sections.html:
File the county's appeal form with the Board of Assessment Appeals, together with a check payable to the County of Luzerne in the amount listed on the county's appeal filing fee schedule. The county then sends written notice of the hearing date, time and place. Separate forms exist for single-family homes, multi-family residential property and vacant land.

The single-family form asks for the facts a board will want to see:

  • The tax map identification number, with map, block and lot.
  • The purchase date and price, plus a copy of the current deed.
  • The assessment under appeal, split between land and improvements, and your own opinion of market value.
  • Annual rent, if the property is rented.
  • The reasons for the appeal, signed under penalty for false statements.

The form states that the appellant agrees to a hearing and a decision after October 31, and that one, two or three board members may hear the case. It also warns that the board may raise or lower an assessment based on the evidence, so a weak appeal can backfire. Ask the Assessment Office for the current year's filing deadline before you start.

sections.h2: What happens when Luzerne County property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The Assessment Office collects delinquent property taxes at the courthouse, but it does not issue tax bills. Anyone paying back taxes in person should go to the Tax Claim Bureau first, which issues a statement for the amount being paid. The county page says it accepts only cash and checks for these payments, and credit cards are refused.

Unpaid taxes can end in a tax sale. County ordinance describes four kinds, upset, private, judicial free and clear, and repository sales, all run by the Tax Claim Bureau or its agent under the Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law (72 P.S. 5860.101 and following). Since March 1, 2026 the bureau or its agent collects a $100.00 fee from every buyer at a tax sale, and the county sheriff collects the same amount at mortgage foreclosure sales. The money goes into a county Demolition and Rehabilitation Fund for blighted buildings. Sales to nonprofits, land banks and government bodies are excluded.

If you are selling a house with back taxes, ask the Tax Claim Bureau for a payoff statement so the title company can list every open year and clear it at settlement.

sections.h2: Why does the county charge an extra fee on deeds?
sections.html:
County Council adopted Ordinance 2026-08 on May 26, 2026 by an 11 to 0 vote. It imposes the $15.00 fee that Act 152 of 2016 allows on every deed and mortgage recorded in the county. The money goes into a separate Luzerne County Demolition Fund, used only to tear down blighted property, and the county must send the state Department of Community and Economic Development a plan within 90 days and a report each year after that.

The ordinance defines blighted property as a property meeting at least three of the criteria in section 5(d)(5) of the state's Abandoned and Blighted Property Conservatorship Act. The ordinance took effect 15 days after adoption, and the Recorder began collecting the amount on July 1, 2026. A seller sees it as one more line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What does the county's housing data show?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts counts 135,055 households and 151,965 housing units in Luzerne County. The county issued 295 building permits in 2025, and 89.3 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Owners with a mortgage report a median of $1,475 a month in selected costs, against $623 for owners without one, and households average 2.35 people. Workers spend a mean of 23.5 minutes getting to work, and the county counts 17,059 veterans. The estimated county population was 332,126 in July 2025, up 2.0 percent from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: What property tax and transfer costs hit a seller at closing?
sections.html:
Closing in Luzerne County involves three separate county-level costs besides the tax bill itself.

  • Recording: the Recorder of Deeds schedule effective November 17, 2025 sets $72.75 for a deed or mortgage, and an extra $15.00 has applied to deeds and mortgages since July 1, 2026 for a county demolition fund.
  • PIN certification: the Assessor's Office certifies the parcel number on every deed and bills its own fee. The Recorder's schedule says to call 570-825-1525 for the amount.
  • Transfer tax: the county's schedule lists a 2 percent total in most municipalities, 3.5 percent in Wilkes-Barre and Pittston, and 2.5 percent in Kingston Borough. Hazleton's total is 2 percent.

On a $174,000 sale, which is close to the median owner-occupied value, a 2 percent total comes to $3,480, and a Wilkes-Barre sale at 3.5 percent comes to $6,090. The purchase agreement decides who pays it, though both parties are liable to the state, so read that clause before you accept an offer.

The year's real estate tax is also divided between seller and buyer. Ask your closing agent how the split is figured, and check that the bill used is for the right municipality and school district.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Luzerne County itself?
sections.html:
Luzerne County formed on September 25, 1786 from Northumberland County. It spans 906 square miles in northeastern Pennsylvania and runs on a council-manager home rule form of government. Wilkes-Barre, with 44,328 people in 2020, is the seat. Hazleton follows with 29,963, then Kingston borough with 13,349, Nanticoke with 10,628 and Pittston with 7,591.

The Wyoming Valley, cut by the Susquehanna River, runs through the middle of the county, and mountain ridges rise on each side. Anthracite mining shaped the towns, and the 1930 population of 445,109 has fallen to 325,594 in 2020. Warehousing along Interstates 80 and 81 now employs many residents, with healthcare, universities and power generation behind it.

Ask your municipal office about any sewer, garbage or permit items tied to your address, since the county pages above do not cover them.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Luzerne County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at 570-825-1540 or file the appeal form with the Board of Assessment Appeals. Include the filing fee check made out to the County of Luzerne.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent Luzerne County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay at the courthouse after stopping first at the Tax Claim Bureau, which issues the statement. Only cash and checks are accepted, and credit cards are not.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Wilkes-Barre?
faqs.a: The Recorder of Deeds schedule lists a 3.5 percent total for Wilkes-Barre. Most other municipalities show 2 percent, and Kingston Borough shows 2.5 percent.

faqs.q: Does Luzerne County charge a fee at tax sales?
faqs.a: Yes. Since March 1, 2026 a $100.00 fee is added to the purchase price at tax sales and mortgage foreclosure sales, paid by the buyer into the demolition and rehabilitation fund.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Luzerne County?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $174,100 as the median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024. Individual towns can differ widely from that figure.
